intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
experiences.description: A family-friendly snorkeling adventure in a protected marine sanctuary teeming with colorful fish and sea turtles. Arrive early to secure entry and enjoy calm, clear waters before crowds build. An indoor education center provides a great rainy-day or midday alternative with marine life exhibits.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Experience
experiences.description: An immersive family cultural experience featuring six Polynesian villages, live performances, canoe rides, and traditional craft demonstrations. The indoor evening luau and IMAX theater make it a perfect option to avoid midday heat while learning about Hawaiian and Pacific Island heritage.

experiences.name: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit
experiences.description: A manageable 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside a volcanic crater offering panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Best tackled at sunrise to beat the heat and crowds. Kids ages 5 and up can typically complete this trail, making it a memorable family achievement.

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium Visit
experiences.description: Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring a walk-through underwater tunnel, Hawaiian green sea turtles, manta rays, and interactive tide pools. This is an ideal indoor midday or rainy-day activity for families, offering hours of educational entertainment while staying cool and sheltered.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa Town
experiences.description: Explore the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore with a self-guided food tour sampling legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical fruit smoothies. Best enjoyed in the cooler morning or early evening hours while browsing local shops and galleries.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit
experiences.description: A manageable 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside a volcanic crater offering panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Best tackled at sunrise to beat the heat and crowds. Kids ages 5 and up can typically complete this trail, making it a memorable family achievement.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 11:20 AM — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, collect baggage and arrange ground transportation to your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park. Note: The provided accommodation is in Buena Park, California, not Hawaii — confirm your Hawaii lodging separately. Once settled, head to the nearest beach or local area to decompress after the flight. If staying in the Buena Park area, visit nearby Knott's Berry Farm surroundings or relax at the hotel pool.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Orangethorpe Ave and surrounding streets for a casual dinner. Walk around Downtown Buena Park or a nearby shopping plaza to get oriented.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing — look for grab-and-go options under $10.
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport food court — budget around $12–15.
meals.dinner: In-N-Out Burger or Panda Express near Buena Park for a budget-friendly meal under $12 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is a travel and recovery day. The listed hotel is in Buena Park, CA — if this is a layover or staging point before flying to Hawaii, use this evening to repack, rest, and prepare for the onward journey. Confirm Hawaii island destination and local accommodation before Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: If flying onward to Hawaii today, depart early from Buena Park to LAX or John Wayne Airport. Aim for a morning flight to Honolulu (OGG/HNL). Upon arrival in Hawaii, check in to your budget Hawaii accommodation (hostel, vacation rental, or budget hotel in Waikiki recommended — e.g., Polynesian Hostel Beach Club ~$40–60/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head straight to Waikiki Beach — it's free and one of the most iconic beaches in the world. Rent a boogie board ($10–15/hour) or simply swim and relax. Walk the Kalakaua Avenue strip to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Waikiki beachfront at sunset. Watch local hula performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free, nightly around 6:30 PM).

meals.breakfast: Airport grab-and-go or hotel continental breakfast — budget $8–10.
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In in Honolulu — a legendary local plate lunch spot. Plate lunch (rice, mac salad, protein) for $10–13.
meals.dinner: Marugame Udon in Waikiki — fresh udon noodles starting at $6–9 per bowl, very popular with locals and budget travelers.

day_by_day.notes: August in Hawaii averages highs around 85°F (29°C) — much warmer than the 16.8°C listed, which may reflect a different destination. Pack reef-safe sunscreen. Rain showers are brief and common; carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit — depart by 6:00 AM to beat the heat and crowds. This 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside a volcanic crater offers stunning panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Entry fee is $5 per person (cash or credit). Wear comfortable shoes and bring water.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, cool off at Kaimana Beach (Sans Souci Beach) — a quieter, locals-favorite beach just east of Waikiki with calm, clear water and good snorkeling. Free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Kapiolani Park for a relaxing evening picnic. Watch local families play and enjoy the open green space near the base of Diamond Head.

meals.breakfast: Bring snacks and water from a convenience store (ABC Stores or 7-Eleven) for the hike — granola bars, fruit, $5–7.
meals.lunch: Ono Seafood near Diamond Head — famous for poke bowls at $12–15. A must-try local experience.
meals.dinner: Pick up groceries from Foodland or Times Supermarket and prepare a simple meal or buy ready-made poke/sushi platters for $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Diamond Head parking or take TheBus (Route 23 or 24) from Waikiki for $3 one-way to save on parking fees. Arrive before 7:00 AM to avoid long queues. Bring at least 1 liter of water per person.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — one of Hawaii's best snorkeling spots. Reservations required in advance (book online at $25/adult, children under 12 free). Watch the mandatory marine education video before entering the water. Snorkel gear rental available on-site for $12–15.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or bus along the scenic Windward Coast. Stop at Halona Blowhole Lookout (free) and Sandy Beach Park — a beautiful but rough-surf beach great for watching bodyboarders.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki. Browse the International Market Place (free to enter) and enjoy the open-air atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Bogart's Cafe near Diamond Head — acai bowls and breakfast plates for $10–14.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the supermarket to eat at Sandy Beach — sandwiches, chips, and drinks for $8–10 per person.
meals.dinner: Goma Tei Ramen in Waikiki — hearty ramen bowls for $13–16, great value for a filling meal.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations sell out weeks in advance — book as soon as possible. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. TheBus Route 22 (Beach Bus) goes directly to Hanauma Bay from Waikiki for $3 each way.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant site. The USS Arizona Memorial is free (timed entry passes required, book online in advance). Arrive early as passes go quickly. The visitor center and exhibits are free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore downtown Honolulu's Chinatown — a vibrant neighborhood with art galleries, local markets, and affordable food stalls. Walk through Oahu Market and browse fresh tropical fruits and local snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Aloha Tower Marketplace on the Honolulu waterfront. Enjoy the harbor views and look for free live music events often held on Thursday evenings.

meals.breakfast: Liliha Bakery — a Honolulu institution open since 1950. Try their famous cocoa puffs and breakfast plates for $10–14.
meals.lunch: Chinatown food stalls — dim sum, Vietnamese pho, or Filipino plates for $8–12 per person.
meals.dinner: Highway Inn in Kaka'ako — authentic Hawaiian plate lunches (laulau, poi, kalua pig) for $14–18. A true local experience.

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is a solemn memorial — dress respectfully and speak quietly. No bags larger than a small purse are allowed inside the memorial boat. Lockers are available for $5. TheBus Route 20 or 42 connects Waikiki to Pearl Harbor.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the North Shore of Oahu — about 1 hour from Waikiki by car or bus. Visit Waimea Bay Beach Park, one of Hawaii's most dramatic beaches with a famous cliff-jumping rock (in summer, waves are calm and safe for swimming).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along Kamehameha Highway through the famous North Shore surf towns. Stop at Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach (Banzai Pipeline) — even in summer the scenery is spectacular. Browse local food trucks along the highway.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Haleiwa Town — the charming surf capital of Oahu. Browse local boutiques, art galleries, and enjoy the laid-back atmosphere before heading back to Waikiki.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a Waikiki convenience store before departing — yogurt, fruit, and coffee for $7–9.
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa or Kahuku — legendary garlic shrimp plates for $14–16. A North Shore bucket-list food experience.
meals.dinner: Matsumoto Shave Ice in Haleiwa for dessert ($4–6), then grab a casual dinner at Kono's Northshore — burritos and sandwiches for $10–13.

day_by_day.notes: Renting a car for this day is highly recommended (~$40–60/day from budget rental companies). Alternatively, TheBus Route 52 (Circle Island) goes to the North Shore but takes 2+ hours each way. Start early to maximize time.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie on the Windward Coast (about 1 hour from Waikiki). The daytime village admission is $20–30 per person and includes access to six Polynesian village exhibits — Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Hawaii, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Great for families with interactive cultural demonstrations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center villages. Participate in hands-on activities like coconut husking, fire-making, and traditional canoe rides included in admission.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki. Enjoy a relaxing evening walk along the beach and watch the sunset from the pier near Duke Kahanamoku Statue.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or hostel breakfast, or pick up items from ABC Store — $7–10.
meals.lunch: Gateway Bar & Grill buffet inside the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with some ticket packages or available for ~$20. Offers a wide variety of Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes.
meals.dinner: Eggs 'n Things in Waikiki — popular breakfast-for-dinner spot open late. Pancakes, waffles, and omelets for $12–16.

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets online in advance for discounts. The evening luau show is an additional $100+ per person — skip it to stay on budget and instead enjoy the free hula show at Kuhio Beach. Saturday farmers markets may be available in Kailua or Kapiolani Park.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Manoa Falls Trail — a lush, easy 1.6-mile round-trip hike through a rainforest leading to a stunning 150-foot waterfall. Parking is $5 or take TheBus. Wear water-resistant shoes as the trail can be muddy. Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lyon Arboretum near the trailhead — a beautiful 194-acre botanical garden with free admission (donations welcome). Perfect for families to explore tropical plants and birds.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kaka'ako Waterfront Park for sunset views of the ocean and Honolulu skyline. Check out the famous Pow! Wow! Hawaii street murals in the Kaka'ako neighborhood — a free outdoor art gallery.

meals.breakfast: Cafe Kaila in Market City Shopping Center — known for creative breakfast dishes, $12–16 per person.
meals.lunch: Prepare a picnic lunch from Times Supermarket near Manoa — sandwiches, fruit, and drinks for $8–10 per person.
meals.dinner: Kaka'ako Kitchen — local comfort food with Hawaiian flavors, plates for $12–16. Very popular with locals.

day_by_day.notes: The Manoa Falls trail passes through a rainforest — rain is common even on sunny days. Bring a light rain jacket and insect repellent. The trail is family-friendly but can be slippery; hold children's hands on muddy sections.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final full beach day at Lanikai Beach on the Windward Coast — consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in the world. Calm, turquoise water ideal for swimming and kayaking. Kayak rentals available for $25–35/hour to paddle to the Mokulua Islands offshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore nearby Kailua Town — a charming beach community with local boutiques, cafes, and a relaxed atmosphere. Browse Kailua Beach Park, another stunning white-sand beach with calm waters perfect for families.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a final evening stroll. Visit the Waikiki Historic Trail markers along the beachfront and reflect on the trip. Watch the torch-lighting ceremony at Kuhio Beach (free, nightly at sunset).

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — famous for their red velvet pancakes and creative breakfast menu, $13–17 per person.
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua — gourmet sandwiches, salads, and local snacks for $10–14.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on the last full dinner — Duke's Waikiki has a happy hour menu with appetizers and drinks at reduced prices (4:00–6:00 PM). Budget $20–25 per person for a memorable beachfront meal.

day_by_day.notes: Lanikai Beach has no public facilities — use restrooms at Kailua Beach Park nearby. Street parking is limited; arrive early. This is a great day for families as both Lanikai and Kailua beaches are exceptionally calm and safe for children.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — wake up early for one last sunrise walk on Waikiki Beach. Pick up souvenirs at ABC Stores (most affordable souvenir option in Waikiki) or the Aloha Stadium Swap Meet if time allows ($1 entry, open Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation and head to Honolulu International Airport (HNL). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and boarding. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii. Reflect on an incredible 10-day budget adventure filled with beaches, culture, history, and family memories.

meals.breakfast: Loco Moco at Zippy's — a classic Hawaiian breakfast (rice, hamburger patty, fried egg, gravy) for $10–13. A perfect final Hawaiian meal.
meals.lunch: Airport food court or pack snacks purchased from a supermarket the night before to save money.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Use any remaining cash on last-minute groceries or snacks for the flight. Return any rental car with a full tank to avoid expensive airport fuel surcharges. Keep a small budget buffer (~$50) for unexpected airport expenses or transportation. Total estimated daily budget per person: $80–120 including accommodation, food, activities, and local transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
experiences.description: A family-friendly snorkeling adventure in a protected marine sanctuary teeming with colorful fish and sea turtles. Arrive early to secure entry and enjoy calm, clear waters before crowds build. An indoor education center provides a great rainy-day or midday alternative with marine life exhibits.

The indoor evening luau and IMAX theater make it a perfect option to avoid midday heat while learning about Hawaiian and Pacific Island heritage.

experiences.description: Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring a walk-through underwater tunnel, Hawaiian green sea turtles, manta rays, and interactive tide pools. experiences.description: Explore the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore with a self-guided food tour sampling legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical fruit smoothies. Best enjoyed in the cooler morning or early evening hours while browsing local shops and galleries.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM via Alaska Airlines. Collect luggage, pick up rental car or arrange shuttle transfer to hotel. Check in early if possible or store luggage at the SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll to a nearby beach to get your first taste of Hawaii. Enjoy the ocean views, dip your toes in the water, and let the family decompress from travel. Visit a local ABC Store or Times Supermarket to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Easy, low-key first dinner near the hotel. Explore the local area and find a casual family-friendly restaurant to enjoy a relaxed welcome meal. Head back to the hotel early to rest and recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport upon arrival — try a local plate lunch spot inside the terminal for your first taste of Hawaiian cuisine.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick and affordable plate lunch from a nearby local diner or food truck — try a classic Hawaiian plate with rice, macaroni salad, and teriyaki chicken (~$12–16 per person).
meals.dinner: Dine at a casual family restaurant near the hotel such as a local Hawaiian BBQ spot or a mid-range chain like Zippy's or Kono's — budget around $15–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11:20 AM, Day 1 is intentionally light. Prioritize rest and orientation. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Pick up a Hawaii travel map or download offline maps for the week ahead. Note: The hotel address listed is in Buena Park, CA — confirm your actual Hawaii accommodation address upon booking.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with the Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit. Depart by 7:00 AM to beat the heat and crowds. This manageable 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside the volcanic crater rewards the whole family with stunning panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Waikiki Beach after the hike. Rent beach chairs and umbrellas, splash in the waves, and let the kids build sandcastles. Consider a beginner surf lesson on the beach — many vendors offer 1-hour group lessons for families at around $40–60 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Waikiki strip and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere. Watch the famous Waikiki sunset from the beach before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light breakfast before the hike — try Leonard's Bakery for fresh malasadas (Portuguese donuts) or pick up fruit and granola bars from a nearby market (~$8–12).
meals.lunch: After the hike and beach time, enjoy lunch at a casual beachside café in Waikiki such as Eggs 'n Things or Duke's Waikiki — try the loco moco or fresh fish tacos (~$15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Marukame Udon in Waikiki — a beloved local favorite with fresh handmade udon noodles at very affordable prices (~$8–14 per person). Expect a short line but it moves quickly.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head State Monument charges a small entrance fee (~$5 per person or $10 per vehicle). Book online in advance as timed entry reservations are required. Bring plenty of water for the hike — temperatures can rise quickly inside the crater. Apply reef-safe sunscreen before beach activities.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for a family-friendly snorkeling adventure. Arrive early (doors open at 6:45 AM) as entry is limited and spots fill up fast. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel in the protected bay teeming with colorful tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive along the scenic southeastern coastline of Oahu. Stop at Halona Blowhole Lookout for dramatic ocean views and wave action. Continue to Sandy Beach Park — a beautiful but powerful beach great for watching local bodyboarders (swimming not recommended for young children due to strong shore break).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area and enjoy a relaxed evening. Visit a local farmers market if one is running nearby, or explore a shopping center for souvenirs and local goods.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab a quick bite at a nearby café before heading to Hanauma Bay — aim to arrive right at opening time.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at Hanauma Bay's picnic area (no outside food allowed inside the preserve, but you can eat in the parking/picnic area). Alternatively, grab plate lunches from a nearby deli or food truck on the way (~$12–15 per person).
meals.dinner: Try Ono Seafood or Ono Hawaiian Foods near Kapahulu Avenue for authentic Hawaiian poke bowls and traditional dishes like kalua pig and poi (~$15–22 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays — if this falls on a Tuesday, swap Day 3 and Day 4 activities. Reservations for Hanauma Bay are required and can be made online up to 2 days in advance (~$25 per adult, children under 12 free). Bring reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are banned to protect the coral. Snorkel gear can be rented on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Oahu's North Shore — about 1 hour from Waikiki. Begin with the Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa Town. Explore the charming surf town, browse local boutiques and art galleries, and sample the legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's or Aoki's. Try local treats like garlic shrimp, acai bowls, and fresh tropical fruit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the North Shore to visit famous surf spots like Sunset Beach and Banzai Pipeline (Ehukai Beach Park). In August the waves are calmer and great for swimming and snorkeling. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beautiful, less-crowded North Shore beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Waikiki via the Kamehameha Highway, stopping at Dole Plantation for a fun family visit — try the famous Dole Whip soft serve and walk through the pineapple garden maze.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy an acai bowl or smoothie from a local café in Haleiwa Town as you begin your food tour (~$10–14).
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck — a legendary North Shore institution serving garlic butter shrimp plates that are absolutely worth the stop (~$15–18 per plate).
meals.dinner: Back near Waikiki, dine at Ramen Nakamura or Goma Tei Ramen for hearty, affordable bowls of ramen — a great family-friendly option (~$14–20 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The drive to the North Shore is scenic and enjoyable. Allow extra time for traffic, especially on weekends. Dole Plantation charges a small fee for the maze (~$8 per person) but the Dole Whip and garden are free to enjoy. August is a great time to visit the North Shore as the ocean is calm and ideal for families.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center for an immersive full-day family cultural experience. Spend the morning exploring the six Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire making, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center. Enjoy the canoe pageant on the lagoon — a spectacular floating parade of Polynesian performers. Watch live cultural demonstrations and let the kids try traditional games and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous Ha: Breath of Life evening show — a breathtaking theatrical performance featuring fire dancing, traditional music, and the story of a Polynesian boy's journey to manhood. This is a highlight of any Hawaii family trip.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departing — the Polynesian Cultural Center is about 35 miles from Waikiki (roughly 1 hour drive). Grab something quick and filling.
meals.lunch: Dine at the Gateway Restaurant inside the Polynesian Cultural Center — enjoy an all-you-can-eat Island Buffet featuring Hawaiian, Polynesian, and American dishes (~$30–40 per adult, less for children). This is included in some ticket packages.
meals.dinner: The Ali'i Luau dinner package at the Polynesian Cultural Center is highly recommended — a traditional luau feast with imu-roasted kalua pig, poi, haupia, and live entertainment (~$120–150 per adult, ~$80–100 per child). Book in advance as it sells out.

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets well in advance online — combo packages including the luau and evening show offer the best value (~$120–180 per adult depending on package). The center is located in Laie on the North Shore. Plan to spend 6–8 hours here for the full experience. The evening show ends around 9:30–10:00 PM, so plan for a late return to the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry or short flight to Maui for a day trip or overnight stay (optional). If staying on Oahu, visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant experience for the whole family. Tour the USS Arizona Memorial, USS Missouri Battleship, and the Pacific Aviation Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Pearl Harbor, visit Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (if open) or head to Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's largest open-air shopping mall — for some retail therapy, souvenir shopping, and people-watching. The mall also has a beautiful beach park adjacent to it.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset catamaran cruise off the coast of Waikiki — a magical family experience with calm waters, beautiful views, and often dolphin or sea turtle sightings. Many operators offer 2-hour sunset cruises with light snacks and drinks.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast at Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — famous for their red velvet pancakes and guava chiffon pancakes. A beloved local brunch spot (~$14–20 per person).
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable lunch near Pearl Harbor at a local plate lunch spot or the café inside the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center (~$12–16 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hy's Steak House or a mid-range seafood restaurant in Waikiki for a slightly elevated family dinner experience — try fresh Hawaiian fish like mahi-mahi or ono (~$30–50 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor admission to the grounds and visitor center is free, but the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is also free (first-come, first-served or reserve online). The USS Missouri and Pacific Aviation Museum charge separate fees (~$30–35 per adult). Arrive early as it gets very busy. The sunset catamaran cruise costs approximately $50–80 per adult — book in advance through operators like Maita'i Catamaran or Na Hoku II.

day_by_day.morning: If you haven't visited Maui yet, today is a great day for a day trip. Fly or take a ferry to Maui and head straight to the Maui Ocean Center Aquarium in Ma'alaea. This world-class aquarium features a stunning walk-through underwater tunnel, Hawaiian green sea turtles, manta rays, sharks, and fascinating exhibits on Hawaiian marine life — a huge hit with families.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the aquarium, explore the charming town of Lahaina (or Kihei if Lahaina is still recovering from the 2023 fires — check current status before visiting). Browse local art galleries, enjoy the waterfront, and visit the famous Banyan Tree Park. Alternatively, head to Ka'anapali Beach for an afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the ferry or flight back to Oahu in the evening, or if you've arranged an overnight stay in Maui, enjoy a relaxed dinner and evening on the island.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a café near the Maui airport or ferry terminal upon arrival — try a local bakery for fresh pastries and Kona coffee (~$10–14).
meals.lunch: Enjoy lunch at Leoda's Kitchen and Pie Shop in Olowalu on the way to or from Lahaina — famous for their savory pies, sandwiches, and incredible dessert pies (~$14–18 per person).
meals.dinner: If staying in Maui: Dinner at Kimo's Restaurant in Lahaina for fresh seafood with beautiful ocean views (~$25–40 per person). If returning to Oahu: grab a casual dinner near the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Maui Ocean Center admission is approximately $35–40 per adult and $25–30 per child — book online for a small discount. Inter-island flights with Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest typically cost $60–120 per person each way. Book well in advance. Check the current status of Lahaina before visiting out of respect for the community's ongoing recovery.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxing morning at Lanikai Beach — consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in the world. The calm, crystal-clear turquoise water and powdery white sand make it perfect for families. Kayak out to the Mokulua Islands (the twin islands just offshore) for a memorable adventure — kayak rentals are available nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Kailua Town for some afternoon exploration. Browse the boutique shops, local art galleries, and pick up some unique Hawaii-made souvenirs. Visit Kailua Beach Park — another stunning beach with calm waters ideal for paddleboarding and swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Waikiki and enjoy a relaxed evening. Visit the International Market Place in Waikiki for shopping and dining, or take a moonlit walk along the beach.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Kalapawai Café in Kailua — a beloved local café with fresh pastries, breakfast sandwiches, and excellent coffee (~$10–15 per person).
meals.lunch: Enjoy lunch at Buzz's Original Steakhouse in Lanikai or grab a casual bite at a food truck near Kailua Beach (~$14–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Teddy's Bigger Burgers or Lulu's Surf Club in Waikiki for a fun, casual family-friendly meal with great burgers, fish sandwiches, and tropical drinks (~$15–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Lanikai Beach is a residential neighborhood — parking can be limited, so arrive early or use the public beach access paths. Kayak rentals to the Mokulua Islands cost approximately $60–80 for a double kayak for 2 hours. The paddle is about 0.5 miles each way and suitable for families with older children. Always check ocean conditions before kayaking.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided snorkel or glass-bottom boat tour along the Oahu coastline for a different perspective on Hawaii's underwater world. Many operators depart from Waikiki and offer 2–3 hour morning tours that include snorkeling at multiple sites, dolphin watching, and sea turtle encounters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Explore exhibits on Hawaiian royalty, ancient Polynesian navigation, volcanic geology, and the natural history of the Pacific. A wonderful educational experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your second-to-last evening in Hawaii with a special family dinner. Treat yourselves to a slightly elevated dining experience to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try a classic Hawaiian breakfast of eggs, Portuguese sausage, rice, and fresh pineapple (~$10–14).
meals.lunch: Grab a casual lunch near the Bishop Museum or at a nearby local plate lunch spot — try Helena's Hawaiian Food for authentic traditional Hawaiian cuisine (~$14–18 per person).
meals.dinner: Celebrate with dinner at Roy's Waikiki or Orchids at Halekulani for a memorable upscale-casual Hawaiian fusion meal — fresh local fish, creative preparations, and beautiful presentation (~$45–70 per person). Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Snorkel boat tours from Waikiki cost approximately $60–100 per adult and $40–60 per child — book in advance. Bishop Museum admission is approximately $25–30 per adult and $18–22 per child. The museum is closed on Tuesdays. Consider purchasing a combination ticket if available. This is a great day to pick up any remaining souvenirs and gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely morning in Hawaii. Take one last walk along Waikiki Beach at sunrise to soak in the beauty of the islands. Swim, collect shells, or simply sit and watch the surfers. Visit a local coffee shop for a final cup of Kona coffee and a fresh pastry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Ala Moana Center or the International Market Place. Pick up local favorites like Kona coffee, macadamia nut chocolates, Hawaiian sea salt, and aloha shirts to bring home. Check out of the hotel and head to the airport with plenty of time.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with wonderful memories of beaches, culture, adventure, and family bonding. Mahalo for an incredible trip!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a beloved local spot — try Wailana Coffee House in Waikiki for a classic diner-style Hawaiian breakfast open early every day (~$12–16 per person).
meals.lunch: Last lunch in Hawaii at Rainbow Drive-In — a legendary local institution serving affordable plate lunches since 1961. Try the mixed plate with kalua pig, lomi salmon, and rice (~$10–14 per person).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time — grab a final shave ice or malasada at the airport for a sweet send-off.

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully and plan hotel checkout and airport transfer accordingly. Honolulu International Airport (HNL) recommends arriving 2–3 hours before departure for international or mainland flights. Return rental car with a full tank to avoid extra charges. Take a final photo at the beach to remember your Hawaii adventure. A hui hou — until we meet again!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
experiences.description: A family-friendly snorkeling adventure in a protected marine sanctuary teeming with colorful fish and sea turtles. Arrive early to secure entry and enjoy calm, clear waters before crowds build. An indoor education center provides a great rainy-day or midday alternative with marine life exhibits.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Experience
experiences.description: An immersive family cultural experience featuring six Polynesian villages, live performances, canoe rides, and traditional craft demonstrations. The indoor evening luau and IMAX theater make it a perfect option to avoid midday heat while learning about Hawaiian and Pacific Island heritage.

experiences.name: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit
experiences.description: A manageable 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside a volcanic crater offering panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Best tackled at sunrise to beat the heat and crowds. Kids ages 5 and up can typically complete this trail, making it a memorable family achievement.

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium Visit
experiences.description: Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring a walk-through underwater tunnel, Hawaiian green sea turtles, manta rays, and interactive tide pools. This is an ideal indoor midday or rainy-day activity for families, offering hours of educational entertainment while staying cool and sheltered.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa Town
experiences.description: Explore the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore with a self-guided food tour sampling legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical fruit smoothies. Best enjoyed in the cooler morning or early evening hours while browsing local shops and galleries.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 11:20 AM — Flight Alaska lands. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to hotel. Check in early if possible at SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the hotel, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the Buena Park area. Visit a nearby shopping center or relax at the hotel pool to recover from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Light exploration of the local Buena Park dining scene. Head to a nearby upscale restaurant for a welcome dinner to kick off the trip.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing.
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or a quick bite at the airport upon arrival.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Catch Restaurant & Bar in Anaheim — known for fresh seafood and a relaxed upscale atmosphere, perfect for the first evening.

day_by_day.notes: Note: The hotel address (Buena Park, CA) suggests this itinerary begins in Southern California before flying to Hawaii. Day 1 is a travel/arrival day. Ensure all Hawaii inter-island flights and hotel accommodations in Hawaii are pre-booked. Pack reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling activities.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Buena Park to LAX or John Wayne Airport. Board flight to Honolulu, Oahu (approximately 5–6 hours). Arrive in Honolulu and check in to a luxury Waikiki resort such as The Royal Hawaiian or Halekulani Hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, head directly to Waikiki Beach for a relaxed first afternoon in Hawaii. Rent premium beach chairs and umbrellas, take a dip in the warm Pacific, and soak in the iconic views of Diamond Head.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along Kalakaua Avenue, Waikiki's famous beachfront boulevard. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere and browse luxury boutiques.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or airport lounge before departure.
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or grab a quick bite upon arrival in Honolulu.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Mer at Halekulani — Honolulu's most celebrated fine-dining restaurant offering French-inspired cuisine with ocean views. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm luxury hotel reservation in Waikiki in advance. Request an ocean-view room for the full Hawaii experience. Average high around 16.8°C (62°F) — evenings may be cool, bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit — Depart early (around 6:30 AM) for this iconic 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside the volcanic crater. The manageable trail rewards hikers with breathtaking panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Book a timed entry permit in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Waikiki and enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the hotel pool or beach. Arrange a private surf lesson with a certified instructor on Waikiki Beach — a quintessential Hawaii family experience.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Hawaiian luau at a premium venue such as the Royal Hawaiian Luau on the beach, featuring hula performances, fire dancing, and a lavish buffet of Hawaiian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-hike breakfast at the hotel — opt for the resort's breakfast buffet or room service.
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch at Orchids at Halekulani, offering elegant open-air dining with ocean views and a refined Pacific Rim menu.
meals.dinner: Royal Hawaiian Luau dinner — included with luau ticket. Enjoy poi, kalua pig, lomi salmon, haupia, and tropical cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head timed entry permits must be reserved online in advance at gostateparks.hawaii.gov. Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring water. The hike is family-friendly but involves some stairs and tunnel passages.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — A must-do family snorkeling adventure in one of Hawaii's most protected marine sanctuaries. Arrive early (gates open at 6:45 AM) to secure entry. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel among hundreds of colorful tropical fish in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along the scenic southeastern Oahu coastline (Kalanianaole Highway), stopping at Halona Blowhole and Sandy Beach for photos. Continue to Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail for stunning coastal views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a relaxing evening. Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the ocean before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before heading to Hanauma Bay.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch — arrange a premium picnic basket through the hotel concierge to enjoy at a scenic coastal stop.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nobu Honolulu — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion cuisine in a sophisticated setting in Waikiki.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations (book at least 2 days ahead at huihanaumabay.com). Entry fee applies. Use only reef-safe sunscreen — it is strictly enforced. Snorkel gear rental is available on-site, but bringing your own is recommended for hygiene.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Experience — Drive approximately 35 miles north to Laie on Oahu's North Shore. Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural activities including fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Polynesian Cultural Center experience with the afternoon canoe pageant on the lagoon — a spectacular floating parade of Polynesian cultures. Explore the IMAX theater and additional exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous 'HA: Breath of Life' evening show — a breathtaking theatrical production featuring over 100 performers, fire dancers, and stunning Polynesian choreography. Book the premium 'Ali'i Luau' package for a pre-show feast.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departing for Laie.
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a generous spread of Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes included in premium packages.
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a premium all-you-can-eat luau feast with traditional Hawaiian dishes, included with the Ambassador package.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ambassador VIP package at the Polynesian Cultural Center in advance for the best experience, including reserved seating, guided tours, and priority access. The full day experience runs approximately 12:00 PM to 9:30 PM. Drive time from Waikiki is about 1 hour.

day_by_day.morning: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa Town — Head to Oahu's legendary North Shore surf town of Haleiwa. Begin with the iconic shave ice at Matsumoto Shave Ice or Aoki's, then explore local boutiques, art galleries, and surf shops. Sample fresh poke bowls, malasadas (Portuguese doughnuts), and acai bowls from local vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the famous North Shore surf beaches — Sunset Beach, Ehukai Beach (Banzai Pipeline), and Waimea Bay. Watch local surfers (August waves are typically calmer, ideal for swimming). Consider a private stand-up paddleboard lesson at Waimea Bay.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Honolulu along the scenic Kamehameha Highway. Stop at a lookout point for sunset views before returning to Waikiki.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departing.
meals.lunch: Self-guided food tour in Haleiwa — try Giovanni's Shrimp Truck (a North Shore institution) for garlic shrimp plates, and sample local treats throughout town.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Senia in Honolulu — a James Beard Award-nominated restaurant offering creative, locally-sourced tasting menus in an intimate setting.

day_by_day.notes: Haleiwa is approximately 45 minutes from Waikiki. August is a great time to visit the North Shore as the ocean is calm and ideal for families. Bring cash for food trucks and small local vendors. Parking can be limited — arrive early or use a private driver.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight from Honolulu to Kahului, Maui (approximately 30 minutes). Check in to a luxury Maui resort such as the Four Seasons Resort Maui at Wailea or Andaz Maui at Wailea. Spend the morning settling in and enjoying the resort's world-class amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium Visit — Hawaii's premier aquarium in Ma'alaea, featuring a stunning walk-through underwater tunnel, Hawaiian green sea turtles, manta rays, sharks, and vibrant reef exhibits. A wonderful family activity with educational marine conservation programming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing evening. Enjoy cocktails at the resort's oceanfront bar while watching the sunset over the Pacific.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Waikiki hotel before departing for the airport.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Maui Ocean Center's Seascape Ma'alaea Restaurant — casual dining with harbor views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spago Maui at the Four Seasons Wailea — Wolfgang Puck's acclaimed restaurant offering innovative California-Hawaiian cuisine with stunning ocean views.

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights with Hawaiian Airlines or Mokulele Airlines in advance. Maui Ocean Center tickets can be purchased online for a small discount. The aquarium is ideal for families with children of all ages and typically takes 2–3 hours to explore fully.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana — Embark on one of Hawaii's most iconic scenic drives along Maui's northeastern coastline. Hire a private driver or rent a premium SUV. Stop at Twin Falls, Garden of Eden Arboretum, Wailua Falls, and the black sand beach at Waianapanapa State Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana journey, stopping at Hamoa Beach (one of Maui's most beautiful beaches) for a swim. Visit the Pools of 'Ohe'o (Seven Sacred Pools) in Haleakalā National Park for a breathtaking natural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return along the Road to Hana (or complete the loop via Upcountry Maui if road conditions permit). Arrive back at the resort for a well-deserved rest.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departing.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch arranged by the resort concierge — enjoy at a scenic waterfall or beach stop along the route.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mama's Fish House in Pa'ia — one of Maui's most beloved and celebrated restaurants, famous for ultra-fresh locally caught fish. Reservations required weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 64 miles one way with over 600 curves and 59 bridges. Start early (by 7:00 AM) to avoid traffic and maximize time at stops. A private driver is highly recommended for families to fully enjoy the scenery without navigation stress. Waianapanapa State Park requires advance reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Haleakalā Sunrise Experience — Wake at 2:30 AM for a guided private tour to the summit of Haleakalā volcano (10,023 feet) to witness one of the world's most spectacular sunrises above the clouds. Wrap up in warm layers as summit temperatures can drop near freezing. A truly unforgettable family memory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by mid-morning for a well-deserved rest. Spend the afternoon at the resort's luxury pool complex or on Wailea Beach — one of Maui's finest white-sand beaches. Arrange a family snorkeling excursion from the beach or book a private catamaran charter.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a luxury spa experience at the resort spa — book family-friendly treatments such as Hawaiian lomi lomi massages. Enjoy a relaxed final Maui evening.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed sunrise snacks and hot beverages provided by the tour operator or hotel concierge.
meals.lunch: Late brunch at the resort's poolside restaurant upon return — enjoy fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, and Kona coffee.
meals.dinner: Farewell Maui dinner at Ferraro's Bar e Ristorante at the Four Seasons Wailea — an elegant Italian-Mediterranean restaurant with oceanfront terrace dining and live music.

day_by_day.notes: Haleakalā National Park requires advance timed entry reservations for sunrise viewing (recreation.gov). Book 60 days in advance as spots sell out quickly. Dress in warm layers — summit temperatures can be 15–20°C colder than sea level. The experience is suitable for older children and adults.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Maui — Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take one last walk along Wailea Beach or browse the resort's boutique shops for premium Hawaiian souvenirs, local art, and Kona coffee to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Maui resort and arrange private luxury transfer to Kahului Airport. Board inter-island flight back to Honolulu, then connect to your mainland flight back to Southern California. Arrive back at Buena Park in the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive home with incredible memories of a premium Hawaii family adventure. Unpack, rest, and relive the highlights of 10 extraordinary days in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — splurge on the full buffet spread with fresh tropical fruits, macadamia nut pancakes, and Kona coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Kahului Airport or Honolulu Airport during layover — try local options such as Maui Brewing Co. or L&L Hawaiian Barbecue.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or a casual dinner near the Buena Park hotel upon return.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for inter-island connections and mainland flights. Confirm all return flight times and arrange airport transfers in advance. Consider shipping any large souvenir purchases home to avoid baggage fees. Keep all Hawaii National Park passes and receipts for potential tax deductions if applicable.
